land.text: Ganzhou: 'Around the years 881 and 882, Ganzhou slipped from the control of the Guiyi Circuit'; in 874 the Wenmo, 'remnant forces of the Tibetan Empire', drove the Uyghurs out of Ganzhou

predecessors.note: The Guiyi Circuit (848-1036, Shazhou/Dunhuang) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the Wenmo hold between 874 and 894 is not described on the pages. Cliopatria draws the whole Hexi land from 860.

land.text: 'There was a pre-existing community of Uyghurs at Ganzhou by 840 at the very latest'; refugees of the Uyghur Khaganate settled in Ganzhou, Suzhou and Shazhou

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Uyghur Khaganate'; people, not land: the khaganate never held the Hexi.

land.text: 'In 1036 the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom was annexed by the Tanguts'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Western Xia row begins in 990 and touches this shape from 990; the Tangut state was proclaimed in 1038 (Western Xia page).

capitals.name: Ganzhou (Zhangye)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Ganzhou (Zhangye)'. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

rulers.name: Pangteqin (Huaijian Khagan)
rulers.note: 'In 894 the Uyghurs led by Pangteqin (Huaijian Khagan) established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom'; died in 924.

rulers.name: Diyin
rulers.note: Won a succession war against his brother Renmei in 924; died 926.

rulers.name: Jingqiong
rulers.note: The page gives two death years for Jingqiong, 975 and 983.

rulers.name: Yeluohe Mili'e
rulers.note: Succeeded in 975 on the page; the reign end is the researcher's reading of the 983 entry.

rulers.name: Baoguo
rulers.note: Succeeded when Guizhong died in 1028; the kingdom was annexed in 1036.

correction.text: years only: the shape holds from 894; 860-893 the Hexi is the Guiyi Circuit's (Ganzhou until 881-882) and the Wenmo's

keyframe_review.note: 860-895 (978 cells, 0.233 M km2; the pages give no area): the kingdom was established in 894, so the shape holds from 894. Before it, 'In 874, remnant forces of the Tibetan Empire known as the Wenmo ... drove out the Uyghurs' and 'Around the years 881 and 882, Ganzhou slipped from the control of the Guiyi Circuit'; the Guiyi page lists Ganzhou and Suzhou among its prefectures by 861. The shape is Zhangye (47 of 47 cells within 60 km), Jinchang, the Alxa plateau (543 cells of Inner Mongolia) and the central Hexi; it lacks Wuwei (0 of 48 cells).

896-910: the same 978 cells. The page names Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou, Shazhou, Liangzhou and Qinzhou as places where the Uyghur refugees settled; it gives no boundary, so the shape stands as the honest precision of the era.
911-921: +2 cells at 96-106.7 E, -1 at 96.3 E; noise. 910-911: the Ganzhou Uyghurs attacked Jinshan (Guiyi) and 'forced them into an alliance as a lesser partner' (no land).

922-925: +4 cells (107.6-108.5 E) and -5 (103.4-105.8 E) on the Alxa fringe; noise. 925: Cao Yijin (Guiyi) 'attacked and defeated' the Ganzhou Uyghurs (Ganzhou and Guiyi pages), no land change recorded.
926-989: +1, -3 cells; noise. The page records only succession, marriage ties and 961 Song suzerainty.

990-1033: +1, -4 cells; noise. The 1008-1010 fights with the Tanguts and the Liao and the 1009 capture of Liangzhou move no cells in Cliopatria (Wuwei is outside the shape); the ledger holds them as a one-year contest.

correction.text: years only: the shape holds to 1036; 1037-1039 the land is Western Xia's

keyframe_review.note: 1034-1039: the kingdom was 'annexed by the Tanguts' in 1036 ('In 1028 the Ganzhou Uyghurs were defeated by the Tanguts'; Western Xia page: 'In 1028, he sent his son Yuanhao to conquer the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom'; 'By 1036, he had annexed both the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom and the Guiyi Circuit to his west'). The shape is right to 1036; 1037-1039 belong to Western Xia.

region.text: Ganzhou (Zhangye) and the Hexi around it

ledger.note: 894: Pangteqin founds the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom. 'In 894 the Uyghurs led by Pangteqin (Huaijian Khagan) established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in Ganzhou'; infobox 'Established 894'. The page names the city; the shape is Cliopatria's.

1009: the Uyghurs take Liangzhou. 'In 1009 the Ganzhou Uyghurs captured Liangzhou.' The Guiyi page has the Tibetan state of Xiliangfu holding Liangzhou by 906; neither page says who held it in 1009 or for how long, so the capture is a contest, not a gain.
1010: the last dated clash. 'In 1010 the Liao dynasty attacked the Ganzhou Uyghurs and defeated them.' Nothing says Liangzhou was lost or kept; the end of the contest is a bridging judgement.

1028: the Tanguts attack the kingdom. 'In 1028 the Ganzhou Uyghurs were defeated by the Tanguts'; Western Xia page: 'In 1028, he sent his son Yuanhao to conquer the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom.' Guazhou surrendered in 1030.
1036: the Tanguts annex the kingdom. 'In 1036 the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom was annexed by the Tanguts'; 'Shazhou surrendered in 1036'; survivors settled in Dunhuang and Guazhou.
1036: the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom ends (infobox 'disestablished 1036'); its land passes to the Tanguts, whose Western Xia was proclaimed in 1038.

wars.name: Wenmo expulsion of the Ganzhou Uyghurs
wars.outcome: Remnant Tibetan forces known as the Wenmo drove the Uyghurs out of Ganzhou in 874; Ganzhou slipped from the Guiyi Circuit around 881-882 and the kingdom was established there in 894.
wars.note: Before the state's birth; no land belongs to the kingdom.

wars.name: Ganzhou attack on Jinshan
wars.outcome: The Ganzhou Uyghurs attacked the Kingdom of Jinshan (Guiyi) in 910 and 911 and forced it into an alliance as a lesser partner; no land is recorded.
wars.note: Guiyi page (paraphrase): in 911 they forced the Jinshan Kingdom into a subordinate alliance.

wars.name: Guiyi-Ganzhou war of 925
wars.outcome: Cao Yijin attacked and defeated the Ganzhou Uyghurs after heavy fighting in 925; in 926 Aduoyu married Cao Yijin's daughter.
wars.note: After a 916 marriage of a Ganzhou princess to Cao Yijin.

wars.name: Tangut and Liao wars against the Ganzhou Uyghurs
wars.outcome: The Tanguts attacked in 1003 and were beaten; the Uyghurs beat them again in 1008; the Liao attacked and defeated the Uyghurs in 1008 and 1010; the Uyghurs captured Liangzhou in 1009.
wars.note: The 1026 Liao defeat 'in battle' opened the Hexi to Li Yuanhao.

wars.name: Tangut conquest of the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom
wars.outcome: Defeated by the Liao in 1026 and by the Tanguts in 1028, Guazhou surrendered in 1030 and Shazhou in 1036; the kingdom was annexed in 1036.
wars.note: Guiyi page (paraphrase): in 1028 the Tanguts defeated the Ganzhou Uyghurs and in 1030 Cao Xianshun surrendered to them.

certainty.note: A string of oasis cities along the Hexi and the Alxa steppe; no page gives a frontier, and Cliopatria's single shape is held for 140 years.

notes:
Pages opened: Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom (twice), Guiyi Circuit, Western Xia (3 distinct pages, budget 5).
Start: the infobox gives 894 (Cliopatria starts 860); the 860-893 years are the Guiyi Circuit's (Ganzhou until about 881-882) and the Wenmo's after 874. The Cliopatria shape is a static 978 cells to 1039, so the only substantive dates are the start and the end: the kingdom ends in 1036 (infobox), Cliopatria 1039.
The Hexi pages disagree on who surrendered in 1030: the Ganzhou page has 'The Guazhou Uyghurs surrendered to the Tanguts in 1030 and Shazhou surrendered in 1036', the Guiyi page has Cao Xianshun surrendering in 1030 and the Western Xia page has the Guiyi Circuit surrendering 'Two years later' (about 1030). The Guiyi Circuit (848-1036, Shazhou/Dunhuang) and its Jinshan Kingdom (910-914) have no Cliopatria row or dossier; the Tang example dossier gives the Guiyi Hexi (848-907) to 'Tibetans' and this Ganzhou row, so the Guiyi Circuit needs a dossier (ea-04 or a gap-filler).
Events other dossiers should carry: northern-song a vassal_start 961 (cp ganzhou-kingdom; 'In 961 the Ganzhou Uyghurs accepted the Song dynasty as suzerains') ending 1036; western-xia a gain 1028-1036 from this state; liao-dynasty the 1008, 1010 and 1026 attacks (no land).
The 1009 capture of Liangzhou is a one-year contest because the pages do not say whether it was held; Xiliangfu (Tibetan state at Liangzhou by 906) has no dossier. Rulers: the page's succession years are inconsistent for Jingqiong (975 and 983). No area on any page, so no infobox comparison. Gazetteer: Guazhou, Jiuquan, Suzhou (Gansu) are not places; none used.
